mechanism: Aspirin may increase anticholinergic effects of oxybutynin through additive effects on gastric motility and potential CNS potentiation; oxybutynin's anticholinergic properties may reduce aspirin's antiplatelet efficacy by decreasing gastric absorption.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic side effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, cognitive changes) and consider separating administration times; assess bleeding risk in patients requiring aspirin for cardioprotection.
